verdict.rationale: Gitea's own site states it is distributed under the MIT license. The source is public on GitHub (go-gitea/gitea), with build and development docs for working with it locally. Community users independently critique the internals of the Go codebase, which shows the source is readable in practice. missing for 10: a direct quote of the repository's LICENSE file, explicit first-party statement linking the MIT license to the GitHub source repo

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Free, self-hosted Git service under the MIT license.
See docs/build-setup.md for prerequisites and docs/development.md for setting up a local development environment, linting, and testing.
They cite migrations that go up but not down, a nonstandard web framework (go-macaron), too much logic in Go templates, and strange error reporting.
